effect: Passes a thousand pages nobody has read by making the reading of them the thing that keeps the lights off.
available_to: Appropriators, at three in the morning, with a shutdown clock on the wall.
counter: A single-subject rule, a mandatory reading period, or a clerk with stamina and a public log.

confused_with.tell: The filibluster stops a bill by talking; the omnibust passes one by making sure nobody can.

senses: The capability of a legislature to bundle everything it cannot defend separately into one document too large to read and too urgent to refuse.

It works because the deadline does the arguing. Every objection can be answered with the same sentence - the government closes Friday - so the bill's contents are never weighed against each other, only against the clock.
example: *"The **omnibust** carried a bridge, a ban, three tax credits and a paragraph nobody has explained, and it passed at 3:41 a.m. because the alternative was a shutdown."*
